- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and prices are trending down, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to capture mean reversion.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior period), model frequently overshoots in subsequent days; apply a 2–5% downward correction to avoid overreaction.  
- If model forecast is significantly higher than recent 5-day average (e.g., >10% above), reduce forecast by 5–10% to reflect mean reversion bias.  
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-period, model often fails to adjust quickly; apply a 1–3% upward correction in the first 3–5 days of sentiment shift.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome deviates >5% from model in first 5 days, apply a 1–2% downward adjustment to subsequent days to account for lag.
